evidence: The claim concerns the upstream mikefarah/yq v4.54.1 release checksum for yq_linux_amd64. Settling it needs the release's checksums file or asset digest, which is not in the source or the supplied artifacts. I had no network access and did not fetch it. Missing evidence: the upstream checksums (or GitHub asset digest) for v4.54.1.

install.sh:12-14 uses curl with --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' and URL https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/$VERSION/yq_linux_amd64 (VERSION=v4.54.1). The flags do enforce HTTPS-only for the initial request and redirects. Whether the asset exists in the v4.54.1 release and whether GitHub's redirect chain is HTTPS-only is external state; I have no network access and the repo holds no release asset list. The asset name yq_linux_amd64 matches yq's known naming convention, but I did not verify it against the release. The SHA256 check at line 15 adds integrity protection.

action.yml:4-7 is a composite action running install.sh with bash. RUNNER_TEMP and GITHUB_PATH are default runner environment variables available to every step, composite steps included. install.sh:8-9 requires both, and :16-19 appends the install directory to GITHUB_PATH. Per documented GITHUB_PATH semantics, this prepends the directory to PATH for later steps in the same job, including steps after a composite action. The consumers are the later 'Read config' steps in move-to-in-progress.yml:25-28 and close-released-items.yml:38-42, which call yq after `uses: ./.github/actions/install-yq`. I did not run it on a runner. The conclusion rests on the documented runner behavior.

install.sh:15 runs the check in a subshell after cd into $DOWNLOAD, where curl wrote 'yq' (line 13). printf emits '<digest>  yq' (two-space text-mode format), so sha256sum --check reads ./yq relative to cwd. On mismatch it prints FAILED and exits 1. A missing file also exits 1. set -euo pipefail (line 2) makes the subshell's non-zero status abort the script before the install on line 18. This matches the documented GNU sha256sum behavior. I did not run the command.

install.sh:15 pipes 'digest  yq' into 'sha256sum --check -' under set -euo pipefail. On a mismatch GNU coreutils prints 'yq: FAILED' to stdout and 'sha256sum: WARNING: 1 computed checksum did NOT match' to stderr. The script does not redirect stderr, so it reaches result.stderr (test_build_inputs.py:71,82). The mismatch case writes different bytes (line 48), so this path is exercised. The message is only translated under non-English locales. The test copies os.environ (line 68) and does not pin LC_ALL=C. A standard GitHub runner uses an English or C locale, so the substring matches there. I did not run the test.

install.sh:12-14 calls bare `curl` with `--output "$DOWNLOAD/yq"` as separate argv tokens. The stub (test_build_inputs.py:51-60) loops argv, on `--output` copies the payload to $2 (the next arg), and exits 0. The test prepends the stubs dir to PATH (line 68), so the bare `curl` resolves to the stub. Earlier flags are skipped by the shift loop, and the network_failure case exits 22 before the scan.

Both workflows have jobs.config (move-to-in-progress.yml:10, close-released-items.yml:22) whose steps include 'uses: ./.github/actions/install-yq' (lines 20, 33) and a step with id: config and a run block (lines 22-23, 35-36).

The claim concerns whether @anthropic-ai/mcpb@2.1.2 is published on npm and what its pack CLI accepts. That is external registry state, not in the repository view. I did not query the npm registry (for example `npm view @anthropic-ai/mcpb@2.1.2`) or inspect the package's CLI.

mcpb/build.sh:73 runs `npx --yes @anthropic-ai/mcpb@2.1.2 pack`. Grep of the head view found no other invocation of the mcpb CLI (only README, build.sh, and a test regex at tests/unit/test_build_inputs.py:20 that accepts any version). No package-lock.json exists under mcpb, so transitive deps are unlocked. Hostile input considered: a second call site (workflow/Dockerfile) with a different pin; none exists.

Grep of head .github shows yq is installed only via ./.github/actions/install-yq, used by exactly move-to-in-progress.yml:19-20 and close-released-items.yml:32-33. install.sh:4-15 downloads a fixed v4.54.1 release and runs sha256sum --check before install. security-audit.yml:198 only allow-lists a yq tool name; no other workflow fetches yq. MCPB CLI is pinned at mcpb/build.sh:73 (@anthropic-ai/mcpb@2.1.2), invoked from mcpb.yml; the CHANGELOG sentence reads as two separate fixes with the 'two workflows' scope applying to the yq verification, which holds. Note: the MCPB pin is not in those two workflows, so the wording is slightly loose.

Grep of .github in head view shows only two users of ./.github/actions/install-yq: move-to-in-progress.yml:20 (job runs-on ubuntu-latest at :11) and close-released-items.yml:33 (job runs-on ubuntu-latest at :23). ubuntu-latest is Linux amd64. No other workflow references the action, so no hostile caller (e.g. matrix/self-hosted arm runner) exists in the repo.

close-released-items.yml:31-42: checkout, then `uses: ./.github/actions/install-yq` (composite, action.yml runs install.sh), then `Read config` in the same job calling yq. install.sh:16-19 installs yq to $RUNNER_TEMP/sqllens-yq-bin/yq (mode 0755) and appends that dir to $GITHUB_PATH. GITHUB_PATH entries are prepended to PATH for all later steps in the job, so the Read config step resolves this yq, and it would take precedence over any image-preinstalled yq. Composite steps' GITHUB_PATH writes persist to later job steps. Nothing in the step depends on /usr/local/bin/yq.

install.sh:2 set -euo pipefail; :10 mktemp -d with quoted "$RUNNER_TEMP/yq-download.XXXXXX" (template ends in XXXXXX, quoted so spaces are safe); :11 trap 'rm -rf "$DOWNLOAD"' EXIT, with the variable expanded at exit and quoted. Bash runs the EXIT trap when errexit aborts the script, so a curl failure (:12) or a checksum failure (:15, the subshell's nonzero status triggers errexit in the parent) both run the cleanup. Normal completion runs it too. Checked by reading the script only; I did not run it or read the test file.
